summary: Agency audit of SFT-stage results: is the API agent validity advantage real, what drives J/P failures, which claims are supported

result.summary:
EXPLORATORY (post hoc). Every number below is from the 1,454-room cohort, scored with the frozen gate. 1,451 rooms are complete for J, P and L (GT is always complete).

**Short answer.** L's advantage over J and P is real. Its advantage over GT, and its 0.935 headline, are inflated by two things: L shrinks furniture, and GT itself fails the gate on noisy sources (3D-FRONT and scans).

**Scoring path (no artifact found).**
- J/P rows from evaluate_llm and evaluate_pair are identical (1,454/1,454 for each arm).
- I re-scored L from the raw API text using J's request: 1,453/1,454 rows are byte-identical. The one difference is the last digit of a float in size_log_mae.
- Re-running the gate on the stored layouts gives 0 mismatches for J, P and L. GT pass/fail agrees with the frozen reference for 1,454/1,454 rooms.
- An independent hand check of 5 rooms × 4 systems matches every out-of-bounds, support and ceiling count.
- L's first answers were all valid, so L-raw and L-harness are identical.

**Size shrinkage.** L's footprints are on average 16% smaller than GT (log bias −0.175, 95% CI [−0.193, −0.159]); volumes are 25% smaller (−0.292). J is at −0.048 and P at −0.023 on the same rooms. Undoing each system's own average bias with the amendment-005 rule:

| System | Success, own sizes | Success, bias removed (a′) |
|---|---|---|
| L | 0.935 | 0.765 |
| J | 0.431 | 0.371 |
| P | 0.510 | 0.515 |
| GT | 0.725 | — |

- After this correction L still leads J by +0.394 [0.359, 0.427] and P by +0.250 [0.214, 0.285], but leads GT by only +0.041 [0.009, 0.073].
- Giving every system the true GT footprints at its own positions: L 0.420, J 0.246, P 0.281, against 0.725 for GT's own layouts. L still beats J and P, but its layouts only pass at its own shrunken sizes.

**Beating GT depends on the source.** L only beats GT where GT itself fails the gate.

| Rooms | n | GT | L | L after bias removal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clean-GT sources (GT ≥ 0.8, excluding holodeck) | 150 | 0.920 | 0.793 | 0.667 |
| Holodeck | 503 | 1.000 | 0.994 | 0.789 |
| 3D-FRONT | 536 | 0.522 | 0.976 | 0.819 |
| Other noisy-GT sources | 265 | 0.502 | 0.819 | 0.668 |

On the 400 rooms where GT fails, L passes 88.3%. Of the rooms where GT fails and L passes, 210 are 3D-FRONT rooms where GT has box-level collisions (some are overlapping duplicate bookcases).

**How L gets its validity.**
- **No overlaps at all:** 0.0055 chair-under-table overlaps per room vs 0.498 for GT; 0.0069 small-inside-large overlaps vs 0.161. Only 3.2% of L rooms have any overlap, vs 36.8% for GT.
- **Keeps away from walls:** furniture sits 0.263 m from the wall on average vs 0.167 m for GT; 47.5% of floor objects are against a wall vs 63.4%.
- **Covers less floor:** 0.292 of floor area vs 0.362.
- It is not clustering objects: average spacing between objects equals GT's (difference −0.0016 [−0.0087, 0.0051]).

**Suspected tricks that turned out false.**
- Not everything is against walls; L is less wall-bound than GT.
- Objects do not face walls: 2.0% vs 2.6% for GT.
- Parent changes are mostly plausible: 24.8% of objects are on another object vs 18.4% for GT, and the most common moves are book on book (33), pillow on couch (25) and cup on table (17).
- The ceiling check is skipped in 690 rooms with unknown height, but L puts no objects above 2.8 m there.
- The only gate loophole L uses is minor: 431 objects predicted under 6 cm tall (which skips the collision check) where GT is taller, mostly books.

**Errors in the findings draft (item 5).**
- It compares L's OOR (0.031) with GT's all-test OOR (0.079). On this cohort GT's OOR is 0.048.
- It reports L's raw success without L's size bias, which breaks the draft's own rule to always report success next to footprint bias.

Scripts and outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-slian-Desktop-3D-Worldedge-OptiScene/f2530c85-f966-4ee4-9e65-58f0d9e9e62c/scratchpad/sftaudit-geomL/: prep.py, analyze.py, extra.py, split.py, results.json, extra.json, cohort.pkl. Run with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPATH set to the repo plus the script folder. Nothing in the repo or data was changed.

findings.claim: L's headline validity (0.935) is inflated by systematic undersizing; the amendment-005 size guard was never applied to L.
findings.evidence: EXPLORATORY. Footprint log bias on 1,451 common-complete rooms: L −0.1754 [−0.1927, −0.1589]; volume −0.2924 [−0.3188, −0.2675]; per axis x −0.060, y −0.116, z −0.117. J −0.0478, P −0.0226, GT 0. L−J footprint −0.1276 [−0.1429, −0.1125]; L−P −0.1528 [−0.1682, −0.1380]. 43.7% of L objects have footprint below 0.8× GT (J 33.7%, P 29.4%). a′ factor for L = exp(0.1754/2) = 1.0916, which drops L from 0.9347 to 0.7655 (−16.9 pp). Scaling L by ×1.10 gives 0.728, about GT's 0.725. For reference, scaling GT by ×0.9 gives 0.800 and ×1.1 gives 0.207. The size log MAE gap (0.300 vs 0.243/0.238) is mostly this shrinkage: orientation-invariant MAE is 0.279, and x/y swaps are only 6.1% of objects (J 3.4%, P 3.0%).
findings.recommendation: Report B_L, volume bias and a′_L beside L's raw success in T5 and in the findings. Add a′ (own-bias rescale, same frozen gate) to evaluate_llm/report_v2 for every agent, using the J/P/L common-complete cohort rooms for B.

findings.claim: L 'beating GT' is mainly an artifact of GT failing the gate on 3D-FRONT and scan sources. Where GT is clean, L matches or trails GT.

Success as GT / L / L a′: clean-GT sources excluding holodeck (n=150) 0.920 / 0.793 / 0.667; holodeck (n=503) 1.000 / 0.994 / 0.789; 3D-FRONT (n=536) 0.522 / 0.976 / 0.819; other noisy-GT sources (n=265) 0.502 / 0.819 / 0.668. verdicts.note:
EXPLORATORY (post hoc). I rebuilt the work independently: GT rooms rebuilt from the export with bind_room, GT scored by g.score through the reference_rows path, and every rescale re-run through g.geometry. Common-complete rooms = 1,451, with 12,760 objects. Reproduced: B_fp L −0.1754 (my simple house-cluster CI [−0.1947, −0.1551]), J −0.0478, P −0.0226; volume bias L −0.2924; per-axis bias L −0.0596/−0.1158/−0.1170; share of objects with footprint below 0.8× GT: L 43.7%, J 33.7%, P 29.4%. a′_L with factor 1.0916 gives 0.7655. L ×1.10 gives 0.7276. GT ×0.9 gives 0.7999 and ×1.1 gives 0.2070.

REFUTED: 'the size log MAE gap is mostly this shrinkage'. Shifting L's log sizes by the best constant per-axis offset only moves its MAE from 0.2997 to 0.2904 (global median offset) or 0.2840 (per-source median offset). That is 16–28% of the +0.057 gap to J (0.2427). Swap-invariance alone removes more: 0.2997 to 0.2792. Swap-invariance plus per-source offset still leaves 0.2634, above J. Most of the gap is per-object scatter, not bias.

QUALIFY 1: the bias is not uniform. L's mean bias is +0.074 on the clean-GT sources (L oversizes there), −0.207 on holodeck, −0.181 on 3D-FRONT and −0.245 on the rest. On holodeck the train prior is itself −0.132 against GT, so holodeck GT assets are larger than corpus norms.

QUALIFY 2: amendment 005 §4 does not pre-register B or a′ for agents, so 'never applied' is a reporting gap against the findings' own lesson, not a protocol breach.

Sensitivity: debiasing with per-source factors gives L 0.7084, below GT's 0.7249. The inflation is therefore 17–23 pp, not just 17.

EXPLORATORY.

Reproduced, as GT / L / L a′ (pooled factor):
- clean-GT sources, n=150: 0.920 / 0.793 / 0.667
- holodeck, n=503: 1.000 / 0.994 / 0.789
- 3D-FRONT, n=536: 0.522 / 0.976 / 0.819
- other sources, n=265: 0.502 / 0.819 / 0.668

Also reproduced: L passes 0.9545 of the GT-pass stratum (n=1,054) and 0.8825 of the 400 GT-fail rooms. GT failure causes: main 255, OOB 43, fixed 18, multiple 84. Of the 247 3D-FRONT rooms where L passes and GT fails, 210 have a GT main collision (163 have main collisions only). il3d:ba95538c has 36 bookcase×bookcase main pairs, and L passes it.

Corrections:
(i) L is below GT in 6 of 18 sources, not 5. Holodeck is 0.994 vs 1.000.
(ii) The a′ column applies the pooled factor 1.0916 to every group. With each group's own L bias the results change: clean group factor 0.964 gives a′ 0.833, not 0.667; holodeck 1.109 gives 0.710, not 0.789; 3D-FRONT 0.802; other 0.580. The clean-group 0.667 is an over-correction.
(iii) 'Treat 3D-FRONT GT gate failures as label noise' is overstated. In failing 3D-FRONT GT rooms there are 462 main pairs. Only 99 (21%) are same-category duplicates; their median overlap is 52% of the smaller footprint. The other 363 (79%) are cross-category adjacencies with a median overlap of 22%: side table×king bed 32, TV stand×potted plant 23, dressing table×bed 18, nightstand×wardrobe 15, desk×bed 13. Many of these are plausible tight arrangements that fall outside the gate's tuck list ('Corner/Side Table' does not match 'night/bedside'). That is gate strictness, not label noise.

The room-level statement 'L only beats GT where GT fails' is true by construction; only the source-level version carries information.

EXPLORATORY.

Reproduced, with J/P a′ using the full-test factors:
- L a′ − J a′ = +0.3941 [0.356, 0.427]
- L a′ − P a′ = +0.2503 [0.214, 0.283]
- L a′ − GT = +0.0406 [0.005, 0.076]
- GT footprints at each system's own positions: L 0.4195, J 0.2462, P 0.2806. With GT footprints, 40.17% of L rooms have an OOB object.

REFUTED: 'they pass at the agent's own shrunken sizes, not at true furniture sizes' and the comparison 'L 0.420 vs GT 0.725'. The test is not symmetric: GT is scored at its own sizes. The reverse counterfactual shows this:
- GT positions with L's footprints: 0.4904.
- GT positions with L's per-object size ratios, room mean bias removed: 0.2916.
Swapping in another system's sizes breaks any layout, GT included. The substitution measures per-object mismatch, not shrinkage; a′ is the shrinkage test.

Also:
- The factor choice is inconsistent: L uses cohort B but J/P use full-test factors. With cohort factors (J 1.0242, P 1.0114): a′ J 0.3941, P 0.4945; L−J +0.371, L−P +0.271.
- The +0.041 lead over GT is not robust: with per-source factors L a′ is 0.708 < GT 0.725.

The L > J/P conclusion stands.

Every rate in F4 reproduced exactly on the 1,454 requests:
- OOB: GT 7.22%, J 13.41%, P 12.24%, L 0.55%
- support: 0% / 3.16% / 1.24% / 3.92%
- ceiling: P 0.41%
- main collisions: 23.04% / 51.10% / 44.09% / 2.41%
- severe collisions: 11.83% / 33.15% / 30.26% / 0.48%
- fixed blocking: 3.71% / 3.71% / 4.54% / 0.07%
- main pairs per complete room: 0.575 / 6.164 / 6.834 / 0.033

Sole-cause counts also match exactly for all four systems.

For the 44 floating wall items (shelf 10, picture 8, …), GT puts 32 on the floor (z=0, no parent) and 12 on a movable parent. L's output also breaks the prompt contract, which says to omit 'on' only for floor support (floor z=0). So these are a contract and data-convention mismatch, not only gate strictness.

verification.overall:
EXPLORATORY (post hoc) independent re-check. I rebuilt the cohort from the GT export and the J/P/L rows, re-ran the frozen gate locally, and changed nothing in the repo or data.

**Numbers.** Almost every number in the agent-validity report reproduces to 3–4 decimals: B_L, a′_L 0.7655, the scaling tests, the per-group success rates, the flag rates, the sole-cause counts, the GT-pass stratum, the strata split, the cohort GT OOR of 0.0481, and the scoring-path identity (0 re-gate mismatches; 1,453/1,454 rows identical on re-score).

**Over-claims to fix before anything goes into findings:**
1. **F1:** 'the size log MAE gap is mostly shrinkage' is refuted. Optimal per-axis debiasing cuts L's MAE only from 0.2997 to 0.2904–0.2840, versus J at 0.2427. Swap-invariance explains more than debiasing does. The gap is mainly per-object scatter.

EXPLORATORY (post hoc). Scored on all 8,647 test rooms. The gate failure rates are J 0.6118, P 0.6104 and GT 0.2770, so the gap to GT is 0.3348 for J and 0.3334 for P.

I split the gap across gate parts with a Shapley split (each part's average contribution over all orders of switching parts off). Overlaps between movable objects ("main" collisions) account for 0.239 of J's gap (71%) and 0.225 of P's (67%). Out-of-bounds (OOB) accounts for 0.040 (J) and 0.066 (P). Support, ceiling and incomplete output together account for 0.032 and 0.020. Blocked fixed objects, mostly doors, account for 0.024 and 0.022. Nothing is left over.

Top 3 drivers:
1. **Floor-furniture overlaps that are mostly severe.** Main collisions occur in 52.2% (J) and 52.4% (P) of rooms vs 21.2% for GT. 80% (J) and 92% (P) of colliding pairs are severe, meaning the overlap covers more than 30% of the smaller footprint. Ignoring only floor-vs-floor pairs raises success from 0.388 to 0.628 for J and from 0.390 to 0.583 for P.
2. **Object count, concentrated in four synthetic sources.** Failure climbs from 0.333 to 0.980 (J) and from 0.312 to 1.000 (P) between 1–5 and 51+ objects, while GT stays between 0.21 and 0.35. Rooms with more than 10 objects are 35.4% of rooms but hold 63.8% (J) and 68.9% (P) of the excess failures. MansionWorld, InternScenes_gen, SAGE-10k and OptiScene_holodeck are 34.3% of rooms, where GT fails 0–13%, but they hold 75.0% (J) and 72.4% (P) of the excess.
3. **Out-of-bounds placement in large rooms.** OOB rates are J 14.9%, P 19.9% and GT 6.8%. In rooms of 60 m² or more they reach 0.397 (J) and 0.505 (P), against 0.032 for GT.

Smaller factors:
- **Doors.** Blocked fixed objects occur in 11.9% (J) and 13.0% (P) of rooms vs 7.2% for GT, with doors about half of the blocked pairs. This ranks fourth.
- **Support failures.** These occur in 5.5% (J) and 3.3% (P) of rooms vs 0 for GT. They are the only failure in just 0.44% (J) and 0.28% (P) of rooms.
- **Boundary type.** It is not a driver: the excess on scanned-hull boundaries (0.25–0.27) is smaller than on wall polygons (0.34).

The audit's "lossless" claim holds. The cm and integer-degree rounding in the request changes no numbers here, because the reference export is already stored at that precision: 0 of 24,955 fixed boxes and 0 of 108,253 GT objects differ. Boundary and height are copied verbatim. Scored both ways, GT gives the same 6,252 passing rooms, identical to the frozen pass list, with 0 disagreements on any gate part. Rescoring J and P against the room's own unrounded fixed objects changes 0 gate results.

About 66% of J and P failures happen in rooms where GT passes. The API agent shows the gate can be passed: on the 1,454-room cohort it has main collisions in 2.4% of rooms, vs 23.0% for GT, 51.1% for J and 44.1% for P.

I reproduced the SFT-stage primary analysis exactly from the server per-room rows. Local report_v2.py and geometry.py hash-match results.json, and the T1 'all' estimates, CIs and p-values are identical. The arithmetic and the Holm adjustment are correct. Most of findings.md's subgroup and mechanism prose goes beyond what the data show, though. The report also prints CIs that the bootstrap design cannot support for the sources with very few house components.

WHAT THE SFT RESULTS SUPPORT (confirmatory, locked primary endpoint J0 vs P0, Holm across (a),(b), single seed, historical test split): neither co-primary shows an advantage for joint size prediction. (a) J 0.3882 vs P 0.3896, Δ −0.0014 [−0.0122, +0.0091], Holm p 0.793. (b) J 0.2861 vs P 0.2817, Δ +0.0044 [+0.0005, +0.0084], unadjusted p 0.033, Holm p 0.066; the Holm-consistent 97.5% CI is [−0.0001, +0.0089]. So J was not more size-accurate than the train-only prior. J being worse is not confirmed, and the gap is about 0.4% either way.

Supported as estimation only: J undersizes (B_J −0.0831 [−0.0945, −0.0725]). Δ(a′) is −0.0508 [−0.0605, −0.0412], but it is a sensitivity analysis with positions held fixed, not the measured performance of an unbiased J. The agent contrasts are supported as CIs only.

The amendment-005 rule computed at SFT would select P (both conditions fail). Amendment 008 makes DPO2 the binding delivery point, so the report's '交付：P' header at SFT is mislabelled.

WHAT IS NOT SUPPORTED:
- "J helps on low-reuse / real scans": SceneSmith supplies +0.0645 of the low-reuse +0.0693. On real scans J's sizes are worse than the prior, Δ(b) +0.0778 [+0.0644, +0.0910].
- "P helps where the prior is near-exact": on holodeck J's sizes are more accurate, and the prior undersizes (B_P −0.132).
- The agent's "conservative placement" story: the agent undersizes far more than J, B_L −0.175 on the cohort vs J −0.048. The GT OOR it is compared against (0.079) is from the wrong population; GT OOR on the cohort is 0.0481.
- "GT-pass leaves conclusions unchanged": (b) reverses sign there, −0.0050 [−0.0088, −0.0010].
- The mechanism claims (imitation caps validity, explicit constraint optimisation, shrinkage learned because the loss ignores collisions) have no supporting evidence in these data.

CI ANOMALIES:
- mp3d has 18 rooms in only 2 house components (16 + 2). Its 'CIs' are the extreme points of a 3-point bootstrap distribution: −0.0625 / +0.0556 / +1.0 with probabilities 1/4, 1/2, 1/4. The +1.0000 bound is the 2-room component drawn twice.
- Scan2CAD is 1 room / 1 component, which gives zero-width CIs. results.json carries a singleton warning, but report.md never prints it.
- MultiScan has 6 rooms in 4 components, and its Δ(a) −0.5 [−1.0, −0.1429] 'excludes zero' anyway.
- MansionWorld (1,313 rooms) and HSSD200 (138 rooms) have only 15 and 14 components.
- The report has no small-n or few-cluster flag in T2, T3 or S1; the only 'N<50' flag is for FID.
- The per-source Δ(a′) column applies the global B scale in every scope.
- The Holm p for (b) is Monte-Carlo-fragile: 0.066 at the locked 2,000 draws, but 0.0496 and 0.0524 at 20,000 draws (seeds 42 and 7).
